$comment: The Contributor Community (/contributing/; /roles/, /pin/ and /contributors/ redirect here). Unlisted (noindex, not linked from the program page) until the board approves the levels. The one idea: The Labs is built by the people who learn here. Learning by doing, applied to The Labs itself: anyone can contribute, and each level means you've worked hands-on in more of its workstreams, major and minor. The page is three chapters, and each cover's promise is paid off by the sections right under it: Start anywhere (the ways in), Go as far as you like (the levels), Yours for good (how the pin is given, active or emeritus, what won't change). The pins are the symbol: one section walks the levels, by scroll or by picking one, with a pin you can drag (live 3D on desktop). Summarises design/research/recognition-system.md. [PLACEHOLDER] marks what's still open. The covers reuse the program page's macro shots of the pin (src/components/JoinCover.astro): chapters[].shot picks the shot (join.json mission[n]); title is this page's tagline.
title: Contributor Community
description: The Labs is built by the people who learn here. Start anywhere, go as far as you like, and what you earn is yours for good.
draft: A working draft. The board hasn't approved the levels or the workstreams yet, and the pins are still being made.

title: Contributor
Community
hero.lede: The Labs is built by the people who learn here. This is how you become one of them.
hero.status: The first pins go to our two steering committees
hero.pinAlt: The Contributing Member pin, turning to follow your pointer

chapters.title: Go as far as you like.

why.title: A community you can actually show up to.

items.label: In person
items.title: Close to home.
items.body: Neighbors, face to face. Not a chat window.

items.label: Side by side
items.title: Beginners and experts, together.
items.body: Learn from people who've done it. Then teach what you know.

items.label: Hands-on
items.title: Learning is the point.
items.body: Every job here teaches you something, and with AI tools you'll build more than you expect.

items.label: Local
items.title: Real problems, real neighbors.
items.body: What you make helps someone you might pass on the street.

start.title: There's no front door.
start.lede: Some people fix a typo in the guide. Some run a room. It all counts, and it all gets written down.

items.label: If you make things
items.title: Make something better.
items.body: A guide, a flyer, a talk, a bit of code. Suggest a change to anything The Labs runs on, and we'll credit you by name.

items.label: If you want a job to do
items.title: Take a role.
items.body: Upskiller, Poderator, Mentor or Ambassador. You'll be trained, then given plenty of practice. Ambassador is open now.

items.label: If you already know your stuff
items.title: Teach what you know.
items.body: Mentor a pod, look over work in your field, and help newer people find their feet. Your time counts, and we'll recognize it.

items.label: Whichever you pick
items.title: Earn the pin.
items.body: When The Labs runs on something you gave, the people who saw it put your name forward.

rings.title: Four levels. Each one means you've had your hands on more of The Labs.
rings.lede: It isn't a ladder you have to climb. Plenty of people find the job they love and stay there for years. But if you want to see how the whole thing fits together, this is the way.

steps.line: Something you gave is now part of how The Labs runs.
steps.how: Your work, your time, or your know-how made a real difference, and your Lab wrote down what it was.
steps.trusted: Vouching for the next person who's ready.

steps.line: You've done it, so you can check it.
steps.how: Hands-on in two major workstreams, with two people who already wear the pin vouching for you.
steps.trusted: Checking work in the areas you know, and helping newer people get there.

steps.line: You've seen every part of The Labs up close.
steps.how: Hands-on in every major workstream, and some of the smaller ones.
steps.trusted: Saying yes to changes in your Lab's playbooks, and mentoring Reviewers.

steps.line: You know how it all fits together.
steps.how: Hands-on across the board. Other Maintainers put you forward, and the board confirms.
steps.trusted: Setting the direction for a workstream. The board keeps the final say.

rings.names: Workstreams and level names are still drafts. Major workstreams (draft): Build Cycle, Learning Pathways, Community & Outreach, Platform (OLOS), Operations & Governance. Smaller ones include events, communications and research. [PLACEHOLDER]

picker.stageLabel: The {rank} pin. Drag, or use the arrow keys, to turn it.

given.title: It starts with the work. It ends with a handshake.

steps.title: Do the work.
steps.body: Give your time, your skills, or something you made.

steps.title: Two people vouch for you.
steps.body: Both already wear the pin. They help you get there, then say that you did.

steps.title: It goes on the record.
steps.body: Your Lab checks it and writes one line about what you did, next to your name.

steps.title: Pinned.
steps.body: At the next regional gathering, in front of everyone. Your sponsors pin it on and say a few words.

given.note: There's no clock on any of this. Take the time it takes, and every kind of help counts.

status.title: Once it's yours, it stays yours.
status.lede: Your level doesn't expire. The only question is whether you're doing the work right now.

items.label: Active
items.title: In the thick of it.
items.body: You hold a seat in your Lab, and the say that comes with your level.

items.label: Emeritus
items.title: Taking a step back.
items.body: You keep the level, the pin, and your voice. When a seat opens, come back.

decides.title: A few things that won't change.
rules: The pin is a thank-you from the community, not a certificate. It says what you did, not what you're allowed to do.
No one can buy a pin, a level, or a vote.
Levels don't come with a vote, either. The boards look after programs, money, people and the brand.
The only way to lose a level is a serious breach of the Code of Conduct.

join.title: Every pin starts with one contribution.
join.lede: Right now, the open door is the ambassador program. Share your story, bring someone to their first workshop, and see what you end up building.

footer.renders: Images of the pin are 3D renders, not photos. The real pins are still being made.
